decisions.selection: OS2 Single-Mode Fiber with OS2 + optical transport/regeneration
decisions.rationale: OS2 single-mode fiber is recommended because 1e+06 m exceeds the assignment's 400 m OM4 band. For this distance, a single 10GBASE-LR/ER optic pair is not a direct-span solution; use a carrier/optical transport design with engineered regeneration/amplification and a verified end-to-end loss budget.
decisions.transceiver_rationale: 10GBASE-T is the copper PHY; 10GBASE-SR uses short-reach multimode optics (850 nm); 10GBASE-LR/ER are single-mode reach classes whose exact choice depends on distance and the calculated optical loss budget.
decisions.reference: IEEE 802.3 (10GBASE-LR/ER; transport engineering required beyond optic reach)

decisions.selection: Distributed enterprise WAN with cloud connectivity
decisions.input_basis: Profile=global_wan; sites=5; buildings=4; endpoints=2000; average endpoints/building=500.00
decisions.rationale: Four cities and a cloud VPC require distributed WAN connectivity, explicit routing boundaries and secure inter-site connectivity.
decisions.tier_rationale: Campus: core/distribution/access separates backbone, aggregation and endpoint access. Metro: provider Ethernet links connect HQ and remote sites with diverse paths where available. Global: distributed WAN routing connects city networks and the cloud routing domain.
decisions.reference: Assignment scenario; IEEE 802.1Q (VLAN tagging) and IEEE 802.1w (RSTP) where applicable

decisions.selection: Multi-Area OSPF (internal) with eBGP where an external AS boundary exists
decisions.rationale: The multi-site or cloud-boundary condition requires a scalable routing design. Use Multi-Area OSPF inside the enterprise routing domain; use eBGP only across a genuine external autonomous-system boundary.
decisions.reference: RFC 2328 (OSPFv2); RFC 4271 (BGP-4) where an external AS peering exists

decisions.rationale: Resiliency was requested for global wan; alternate connectivity and an explicit failover test plan are recommended.

Summarization reduces inter-domain route table size, but the input only supplies one overall address pool and no site-to-prefix allocation. A safe per-site summary cannot be emitted until non-overlapping site aggregates and route ownership are defined.
decisions.reference: Assignment Global WAN requirement: route summarization

decisions.input_basis: VLAN 10 IOT, VLAN 20 OPERATIONS, VLAN 30 SERVERS, VLAN 99 MANAGEMENT
decisions.rationale: VLANs are taken from the scenario's explicit segmentation requirements; unique IDs and names are validated.

Choose h=11 host bits so 2^11 - 2 >= 1500; prefix = 32 - 11 = /21. The block has 2048 addresses and 2046 conventional usable addresses. Gateway is first usable 10.30.0.1; utilization = 1500/2046 x 100 = 73.31%.
decisions.reference: RFC 950 (Internet Standard Subnetting Procedure); RFC 4632 (CIDR); IPv4 network/broadcast reservation for conventional LAN subnets

topology_caveats: Exact hub/mesh design depends on traffic and provider requirements.
IPsec and cloud routing parameters must be supplied.
routing_caveats: The assignment allows Multi-Area OSPF or eBGP for this condition; the precise choice depends on whether the peer is in the same or a different AS.
redundancy_actions: Provide redundant WAN or VPN termination where supported.
Define routing convergence and failover policy.
Test tunnel failure and alternate-path recovery.
engineering_assumptions: VLSM gateway policy is first usable IPv4 address.
Conventional LAN subnetting reserves network and broadcast addresses.
Media distance bands follow the assignment; final optics require compatibility and optical-budget verification.
Recommendations are design outputs and do not prove live network performance.
